publications.title: Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian Direct Investment Entities for 2025-26
publications.summary: Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-26 1 round of the annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct investment. The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports. publications.title: Sectoral Deployment of Credit by NBFC – September 2026
publications.summary: Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) for the month of September 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement 1 . On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs' credit registered a growth of 15.4 per cent in September 2026 as compared to 13.3 per cent a year ago. Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended September 30, 2026, are given below: Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.8 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as against 5.2 per cent a year ago. Credit growth in industry sector declined to 7.4 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 as compared with 10.2 per cent in September 2025. publications.title: The not-so-fine print: making consumer contracts fair
publications.summary: How many of us read the terms and conditions of a contract before buying a financial product?Contracts hold the detail that shapes everyone's financial life, whether you're taking out a loan, insuring your holiday, or signing up for a crypto wallet.All firms are responsible for making sure that terms in their consumer contracts comply with the fairness and transparency requirements of the Consumer Rights Act (CRA) 2015. When those terms don’t comply, our Consumer Contracts team has powers to challenge firms directly.This work shows how we use the full range of powers Parliament has given us, not only those in financial services legislation, to tackle harm.Here's why it matters: if a term is found to be unfair, it's not just unenforceable – consumers may be due redress too.
